evidence: Ingested data/training_data.csv into Hopsworks feature group `leak_check` (v1, 800 rows) and built feature view `leak_fv_all`, then read the full labeled dataset back through the platform's Feature Query Service. Class-conditional analysis of the platform-returned data shows f2 perfectly separates the binary label with a clean gap and zero overlap: for label=1, f2 ranges [2.03, 3.00] (all 277/277 values >= 2.03); for label=0, f2 ranges [-0.45, 0.58] (all 523/523 values <= 0.58). A single threshold at f2 ~= 1.0 classifies all 800 rows with 0 errors. Every other feature (f1, f3, f4, f5, f6) is ~50% positive in both classes, consistent with genuine N(0,1) features. f2 is therefore computed from the post-outcome label (shifted by ~+2.5 when label=1), leaking the outcome. Note: the `hops sql` (Trino) aggregation path could not read this cached feature group's offline format (rejected as 'Not a Hudi table' / 'Not an Iceberg table', and no Hive/Delta catalog is exposed), so correlation was assessed via the working HQS read path instead.
